## Benchmark Results: .NET 9 vs .NET 10

| Method | .NET 9 (ns) | .NET 10 (ns) | Speedup | Alloc |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **AverageWordLength_Small** | 205.3 | 36.3 | **~5.7×** | 0 B |
| **AverageWordLength_Large** | 8,659.0 | 1,960.7 | **~4.4×** | 0 B |
| **WordLengthHistogram_Small** | 278.2 | 61.7 | **~4.5×** | 88 B |
| **WordLengthHistogram_Large** | 13,212.6 | 5,412.3 | **~2.4×** | 96 B |
| **UniqueWordCount_Small** | 723.5 | 475.4 | **~1.5×** | 760 B |
| **UniqueWordCount_Large** | 46,245.6 | 24,063.5 | **~1.9×** | 73,152 B |

**Summary:** .NET 10 shows significant performance improvements across all three methods — **2–6× faster** — with **zero change in memory allocations**. The upgrade is a clear win. The largest gains are in `AverageWordLength` and `WordLengthHistogram`, likely from JIT improvements in `ReadOnlyCollection<T>` indexer devirtualization and loop optimizations.

> **Caveat:** `ShortRun` (3 iterations) was used and the machine may be under load, so error margins are wide. The directional trend is consistent across all benchmarks though.

The benchmark project is in `Benchmarks/`. Full BDN reports are in `Benchmarks/BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts.net9/` and `Benchmarks/BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts/`.
